With perfect play this is side to move wins (mate in about 7 moves). Best moves: Qd7, Qd8, Kd2, Ke2. Plan: use the queen to shrink the box around the enemy king (stay a knight's move away to avoid stalemate), walk your own king up, then mate on the edge. Next: Play this position against the engine until you win (or hold) it twice in a row.

With perfect play this is side to move wins (mate in about 21 moves). Best moves: Rd1+, Rc4, Rc5, Rb1. Plan (Lucena): get your rook to the 4th rank to "build a bridge", so your king can step out and the rook blocks the checks. Next: Play this position against the engine until you win (or hold) it twice in a row.

With perfect play this is side to move wins (mate in about 11 moves). Best moves: Kd6, Kf6. Plan: the defending king keeps the opposition (kings face each other with one square between, and the other side must move). With White to move here, Black can always answer and draw; if Black had to move, White would win. Next: Play this position against the engine until you win (or hold) it twice in a row.

With perfect play this is a draw. Best moves: Ra2, Ra3, Ra4, Rb6. Plan (Philidor): keep the rook on the 6th rank to stop the white king advancing; once the pawn moves forward, swing the rook back and check from behind.
